# Teardown Index

**Which countries' firms make the foreign electronics inside Russia's weapons.**

**Author:** Thomas Di Domenico · Edition 1.1 · GUR snapshot 30 October 2026

**Live page:** https://thomasdido08-code.github.io/teardown-index/

<!-- HEADLINE:START (generated by scripts/build.py, do not edit by hand) -->
**Traced to parent companies, EU firms make 14.5% of the weighted foreign parts in Russian weapons** (90% range 13.2% to 15.9%), second only to the United States (65.7%). GUR's own headquarters labels put the EU at 5.0%.

Based on 6,252 components in 99 weapon families (GUR snapshot 2026-10-30). 40.2% of dated parts were made in 2022 or later.
<!-- HEADLINE:END -->

## What this measures

Ukraine's military intelligence (GUR) publishes every foreign component it has recovered from Russian weapons, with the manufacturer and the country where the manufacturer is headquartered. The Teardown Index turns that list into a country score:

1. **Count once per weapon type.** Airframes and missiles of the same model are merged into weapon families, so heavily studied weapons don't dominate.
2. **Weight by criticality.** Each part takes the weight of its tier on the Common High Priority List used by the EU, US, UK and Japan: integrated circuits ×4, navigation and radio modules ×3, discrete and passive parts ×2, everything else ×1.
3. **Trace to owners.** GUR's headquarters labels are mapped to the parent group that owns the brand (for example STMicroelectronics to France and Italy, Infineon's US units to Germany).

```
index(country) = weighted parts from that country's firms ÷ all weighted foreign parts
```

A 90% range comes from resampling the weapon families 1,000 times. Three attribution methods are published (parent group, strict ownership and GUR's listed headquarters), so readers can see how much the choice matters.

The index measures **brand exposure in recovered weapons**. It does not measure trade volumes, supply routes or who shipped the parts: most of these parts reach Russia through distributors in third countries.

Full method, validation and open questions: [METHODOLOGY.md](METHODOLOGY.md).

## Main limitations

- **Sampling.** Counts reflect what GUR chose to take apart and publish. Family-level counting and resampling reduce this but do not remove it.
- **Source.** GUR is the intelligence service of a country at war. Its attributions are treated as claims and tested (photo spot-check, marking check, cross-check against RUSI's 2022 teardowns).
- **Attribution choices.** The even STMicroelectronics split and keeping EPCOS under Germany in the headline method are choices; the strict method shows their effect.
- **Tiers** are assigned from GUR's part names by keyword, so some parts are misfiled.
- **Size adjustment** uses total 2021 revenue as a stand-in for market share in the parts Russia buys.

## Repository layout

```
index.html                 the report page (open locally or via GitHub Pages)
data/raw/                  the published index tables (see data/README.md)
data/raw/gur/              the GUR snapshot the tables are built from
data/pipeline/             lookup tables: weapon families, owners, tiers, chipmakers
data/derived/headline.json headline figures, written by scripts/build.py
scripts/build.py           checks the tables and recomputes the headline figures
scripts/pipeline/          scraper and scoring code that rebuilds data/raw/ from GUR
METHODOLOGY.md             full method, validation, limits and open questions
assets/                    bundled d3 library and fonts
```

The tables in `data/raw/` are the output of the scoring pipeline in `scripts/pipeline/`, run on the GUR snapshot of 30 October 2026 in `data/raw/gur/`. See [scripts/pipeline/README.md](scripts/pipeline/README.md) to rebuild them from the snapshot or from a fresh scrape.

## Reproduce

Requires Python 3 only (no packages):

```
python scripts/build.py                                                   # headline from the tables
python scripts/pipeline/score.py data/raw/gur/gur_components_2026-10-30.csv  # tables from the snapshot
```

To view the page locally, run `python -m http.server` in the repository folder and open http://localhost:8000.
